title: Full Workshop: Setting Yourself Up for Success —Jason Liu, OpenAI Codex
talk_summary: The transferable core is persistent per-project context files, scheduled re-waking of the same thread instead of new sessions, and cheap/low-reasoning models for routine loops.

takeaways.technique: Git-tracked markdown memory vault with per-project and per-person files
takeaways.what_they_do: Keeps a monorepo of markdown: one dir per workstream (with links to relevant Slack channels, repo, people) and one file per person (emails, handles, what they work on). Agents read these files instead of being re-prompted; he reviews changes via git diff.
takeaways.evidence_quote: every project file has a link to every slack channel this project is relevant for. And the model will just see that and you go read those slack channels

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of each automation creating a fresh thread, a scheduled message is injected into the same pinned thread so it accumulates context and keeps working a task (e.g. keep a PR rebased and CI green until merged).
takeaways.evidence_quote: the right design is scheduling these messages into the same thread ... keep an eye on this pull request anytime there's feedback fix it

takeaways.technique: Default to low/medium reasoning; reserve high effort for hard tasks
takeaways.what_they_do: He explicitly avoids 'X high maximalists': routine loops (chief of staff, form-filling, coupon search) run at low/medium thinking, and high effort is only for genuinely hard generation.

takeaways.technique: Self-editing skills built from one manual run
takeaways.what_they_do: Do a task once, tell the agent to write a skill from it, and grant permission to edit the skill file when it learns something new; skills are shared as plugins once proven over ~2 months of personal use.
takeaways.evidence_quote: every time you run this skill, you're allowed to edit yourself. If you learn something new, you can edit the skill file

takeaways.technique: Monitor thread spawns and messages sub-threads for triage
takeaways.what_they_do: A single monitor thread watches feedback channels; on an issue it creates a new thread to triage, and if the issue recurs it messages the existing downstream thread rather than duplicating work. Threads can list/rename/message each other.
Capturing an app's accessibility tree alongside the image gives IDs (channel ID, user IDs) so the agent needs one tool call instead of OCR plus several lookup hops.
takeaways.evidence_quote: with appshots, it takes not only the image but the entire accessibility tree of the app ... it's only one function call
